panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Panel-specific caption attributes solitary violaceous hyperkeratotic plaque on limb to M. marinum; article title Fish tank granuloma caused by Mycobacterium marinum. Morphology matches verrucous granulomatous plaque vocabulary. B: Caption attributes multiple violaceous plaques on limbs to M. marinum; linear arrangement along leg visible is sporotrichoid lymphangitic spread. C: Panel-specific caption directly describes warty verrucous plaque on hand as M. marinum cutaneous manifestation. D: Panel-specific caption attributes erythematous swelling of finger with pus discharge to M. marinum; no exact vocabulary key covers purulent finger swelling, so captured as proposed finding with in-text support ulcerative wounds with purulent discharge.
panels.attribution_text: Wu et al. Fish tank granuloma caused by Mycobacterium marinum.. PloS one 2012. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0041296. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Cutaneous manifestations of Mycobacterium marinum infections. Footnote: M. marinum skin infections presented with (A) a solitary, or (B) multiple violaceous plaques with hyperkeratotic surface on limbs. The disease also presented as (C) a warty, verrucous plaque with an irregular border on hand, or (D) erythematous swelling of finger with pus discharge.
in_text_mentions: These patients did not consult a doctor until the symptoms worsened; the duration from the onset of symptoms to visiting a doctor varied from 15 days to as long as 3 years. The most common presentations were tender, erythematous nodules or plaques (18/27). Seven of the 27 patients presented with ulcerative wounds with a purulent discharge (figure 1). One of these patients had corneal involvement and complained of right-eye pain and photophobia, and another patient had dyspnea.

panels.rationale: Single clinical photo of 54-year-old male left hand-forearm with well-demarcated ulcers and multiple nodular granulomatous lesions in linear lymphangitic distribution; article title is Mycobacterium marinum Infection and caption describes classic sporotrichoid spread.
panels.attribution_text: Yasuda et al. Mycobacterium marinum Infection Leading to HIV Diagnosis: A Case Report.. Cureus 2024. doi:10.7759/cureus.73016. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Clinical presentation A well-demarcated skin ulcer surrounded by erythematous tissue, with multiple nodular and granulomatous lesions, extending from the patient's left hand to the forearm.
in_text_mentions: A 54-year-old male noticed a gradually enlarging skin ulcer on his left upper limb. Initially, he visited a local clinic where sporotrichosis was suspected based on the linear pattern of the ulcer, and he was prescribed oral itraconazole for one month. However, the condition did not improve; therefore, he was referred to our hospital to evaluate his skin eruption. Upon examination, he presented with a well-demarcated skin ulcer surrounded by erythematous tissue with multiple roundish ulcers resembling a nodular granulomatous pattern (Figure 1).

plate_findings.evidence: Histological examination of the lesion shows a hyperplastic epidermis and a dense cell infiltrate in the dermis

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Low-power histology of skin biopsy from case of cutaneous M. marinum infection showing hyperplastic epidermis and dense dermal infiltrate consistent with suppurative granulomatous inflammation. B: Higher magnification histology of same M. marinum skin biopsy showing polymorphous infiltrate with macrophages, neutrophils and multinucleated giant cells surrounding pre-necrotic foci, classic suppurative granuloma. C: High-power histology of same M. marinum skin biopsy showing granulomatous infiltrate with multinucleated giant cells and pre-necrotic areas, consistent with suppurative granulomatous inflammation.
panels.attribution_text: Assiri et al. Cutaneous Mycobacterium Marinum Infection (Fish Tank Granuloma) in a Renal Transplant Recipient: Case Report and Literature Review.. Cureus 2019. doi:10.7759/cureus.6013. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: Microscopic examination of the skin biopsy A) Histological examination of the lesion shows a hyperplastic epidermis and a dense cell infiltrate in the dermis; B-C) On higher magnification, the infiltrate consists of lymphocytes, macrophages, neutrophils, and multinucleated giant cells. The dermis contains granular, basophilic, pre-necrotic areas.
in_text_mentions: Microscopic examination of the skin biopsy showed a hyperplastic epidermis and a dense polymorphous dermal infiltrate made of lymphocytes, macrophages, neutrophils, and multinucleated giant cells, occasionally surrounding pre-necrotic foci in the mid-dermis (Figure 2A-C).
